clue.text: Wood may score when correctly placed

indicators.note: the letters of 'may score' are out of order and must be put in their right places

explanation.surface: A footballer or batsman might score if positioned in the right spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycamore is a tree whose timber is used by woodworkers, so it names a type of wood.

clue.text: Harry's artist embraced by girl invited to garden

definitions.note: read as 'harry is': to harry means to raid or plunder, a verb

indicators.note: the artist's letters are held inside the girl's name as in a hug

parts.note: Tennyson's poem begins 'Come into the garden, Maud', so the girl is Maud
RA, a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter belonging to someone named Harry is hugged by a young woman asked into the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts RA inside MAUD. The 's on Harry stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To maraud is to roam raiding and plundering, which is what harrying a territory means.

clue.text: Adherents ask for enigmatic book

indicators.note: puzzling or obscure, so the letters of 'Adherents ask for' are scrambled into a mysterious new order

explanation.surface: Followers request a mysterious volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad's novella about a voyage up the Congo is a famous book.

clue.text: Playwright born an American Indian

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw, the Irish dramatist
née, used before a woman's maiden name

explanation.surface: A dramatist was born a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shawnee are a Native American people originally of the Ohio valley, so one of them fits.

clue.text: Energy in pop produces dance step

indicators.note: the energy letter is placed within the word for pop

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Adding energy to pop music creates a dance move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pop' looks like music but is dad.
explanation.definitionFit: The feather step is a basic figure of the ballroom foxtrot.

clue.text: Impressed by Shuttle's last uncontrolled flight

parts.note: to impress a mark is to stamp it, so impressed means stamped

indicators.note: only the final letter of the shuttle's word is wanted here

explanation.surface: Someone impressed by the end of a space shuttle's chaotic flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a panicked headlong rush of animals or people, a flight out of control.

clue.text: Romeo appears in simple book's outline

indicators.note: the Romeo letter shows up inside the word for simple

parts.note: simple in the sense of foolish, which is daft
R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo turns up in an outline of a simple-minded book.
explanation.definitionFit: A first draft is a rough outline of a book before it is polished.

clue.text: Pink and black stuff on banks of river

indicators.note: the coal lies on either side of the river letter, like its two banks

parts.note: coal is the black stuff dug from a mine
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Pink and black material lies along a riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral is a pinkish-orange colour named after the sea creature's skeleton.

clue.text: General hitch dogs woman of the night

indicators.note: the hitch word follows the woman word closely, like a dog at heel

parts.note: tom is a slang word for a prostitute
to hitch a lift is to thumb one

explanation.surface: An army general's problem is pursuing a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' is not an adjective but the title of the tiny showman Charles Stratton, billed by Barnum as General Tom Thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of Barnum's famous midget performer, so it is a general's name.

clue.text: Receiving hot tip that almost makes one solvent

indicators.note: the tip and shortened that take in the hot letter

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's best tip of the day

indicators.note: the word that is cut short by one final letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Getting a hot tip that nearly makes someone solvent financially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THAT to THA; 'Receiving' puts H into NAPTHA. 'solvent' looks financial but is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Naphtha is a volatile petroleum liquid used to dissolve substances, a chemical solvent.

clue.text: Screen star in final appearance, good to go

indicators.note: the good letter is to leave the phrase

parts.note: a swan song is a performer's farewell performance

explanation.surface: A film star's farewell performance, and a good time to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood film star, famous for Sunset Boulevard.

clue.text: Looking for teachers to employ in historic county

parts.note: to be looking for something is to be hunting it
dons are university teachers
to hire someone is to employ them

explanation.surface: Searching for teachers to take on in an old English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntingdonshire was an English county, now absorbed into Cambridgeshire, so it is a former shire.

clue.text: Refusing to communicate as lead character in Psycho?

definitions.meaning: the leading letter P of the word Psycho is not pronounced

explanation.surface: Mute, like the lead in Hitchcock's Psycho.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead character' suggests Norman Bates, but it is the first letter, P, which makes no sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who will not communicate keeps quiet, and an unpronounced letter is likewise mute.

clue.text: Swallow meat regularly for disciplinarian

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family

indicators.note: every other letter of meat is taken

explanation.surface: Swallowing meat on a regular basis makes a strict figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallow' reads as a verb but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict enforcer of rules, named after a stern French drillmaster.

clue.text: School doctrine being unspecified causes rift

parts.note: an ism is any doctrine or belief, without saying which

explanation.surface: A school's vague doctrine causes a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split within a group, especially a church, so it is a rift.

clue.text: Make-up case

definitions.meaning: a person's make-up is their nature or temperament
a case is an eccentric, an odd person

explanation.surface: A cosmetics bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Character means one's nature, and a 'real character' is an eccentric, just as a 'real case' is.

clue.text: Word used for another top school year's in mass medium

indicators.note: the school and year letters sit within the two M letters

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium
Eton is England's best-known public school
Y abbreviates year; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A top school's year group appears in the mass media.
explanation.definitionFit: A metonym is a substitute word, like 'the Crown' for the monarch, standing for something related.

clue.text: Search with intent to steal weapon

definitions.meaning: to ransack through drawers looking for things to take

explanation.surface: Hunting for a gun to take.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through belongings is to ransack them, and a rifle is also a firearm.

clue.text: Difficult militarist losing head with charge

indicators.note: the militarist word drops its first letter

parts.note: a hawk is someone favouring military action
a ward is someone in another's care, a charge

explanation.surface: A troublesome warmonger beheaded on a criminal charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward means hard to handle or deal with, a close synonym of the definition.

clue.text: A Hebrew beer and where to get it?

definitions.note: a single Hebrew letter, a noun

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
PH is the abbreviation for public house, where beer is sold

explanation.surface: A Jewish man's beer and the place to buy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Hebrew' looks like a person but means a Hebrew letter; the A belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: Separate, close to land, is Minoan island

indicators.note: the close, or end, of the word land is taken

parts.note: Crete was home to the Bronze Age Minoan civilisation

explanation.surface: Something lying apart, near land, is the Minoan island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to land' reads as 'near land' but means the last letter of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means distinct and individually separate, as in discrete units.

clue.text: Rope choking female — male's no time for lesson

indicators.note: the rope is wound round the female letter as if strangling it

parts.note: a halter is a rope for leading a horse
M abbreviates male; the 's means 'is'

explanation.surface: A rope strangles a woman; the man has no time for lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-term is a short school holiday midway through a term, when no classes are held.

clue.text: Break up top class when head departs

indicators.note: the first letter of the combined words goes

parts.note: top means best, the finest
a range is a class or category, as in a price range

explanation.surface: A top class splits up once the headteacher leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when head departs' removes B from BESTRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to alienate them from one another, causing a break-up.

clue.text: Right to go in for confession

definitions.meaning: permission to enter, as with an entry ticket

explanation.surface: Permission to enter for the purpose of confessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission means both being allowed entry and owning up to something.

clue.text: Plant in a container like this

parts.note: a can is a metal container
thus means in this way

explanation.surface: A potted plant, shown like this.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant whose leaves inspired Corinthian capitals.

clue.text: European national valiant in struggle

indicators.note: the letters of valiant are thrown about as in a fight

explanation.surface: A brave European in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latvian is a citizen of Latvia, a Baltic European country.

clue.text: Leading group supplies listening equipment

parts.note: head as an adjective means leading or chief
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: The top team provides audio gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A headset is a pair of headphones, often with a microphone, used for listening.

clue.text: Worthless person's joined religious faction

parts.note: to be in is to be part of, having joined
a sect is a breakaway religious group

explanation.surface: A good-for-nothing has signed up to a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after person means 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an insect is a figurative insult for a contemptible, insignificant person.

clue.text: Jury members find fault with Picasso's article

parts.note: critics pan a show when they slate it
el is Spanish for 'the', and Picasso was Spanish

explanation.surface: A jury criticises Picasso's essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like writing but is the grammatical word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury is a panel of people chosen to judge a case.

clue.text: Scotswoman's husband working in South Africa

indicators.note: the husband and working letters go within the South Africa abbreviation

parts.note: on means functioning, working

explanation.surface: A Scottish woman's husband has a job in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Shona is a common Scottish girl's name, the Gaelic form of Joan.
